source.authors: Andonov K, Dyugmedzhiev A, Lukanov S, Vacheva E, Popgeorgiev G, Nedeltcheva-Antonova D, Naumov B
source.title: Behavioral effects of long-chained ketones in Vipera ammodytes: an experimental approach

value: adult male nose-horned vipers reacted more strongly to a 1:1 mixture of 2-pentacosanone and 2-heptacosanone than to heptacosane, n-hexane or a blank control paper towel
units: categorical (Bayesian zero-inflated GLMM contrasts on counts of chin-rubbing bouts and positive interest scores; significance by highest posterior density interval)
method: terrarium bioassay: paper towel carrying 0.20-0.25 ml of a 1 mg/ml n-hexane solution (about 0.2-0.25 mg) of 2-pentacosanone (C25), 2-heptacosanone (C27), an equal mixture of both, heptacosane (C27 alkane) or n-hexane alone, or a blank towel, left in the individual's terrarium for 10 min and video-recorded; interest, chin-rubbing, general and specific tongue-flick rates scored; each snake received each stimulus three times in random order at least one day apart
conditions: wild-sourced: adults caught in April 2022 and April 2023 from one population near Karlukovo, NW Bulgaria, held in captivity no more than two months and released at the capture sites; 15 adults (8 males, 7 females), 270 tests (144 male, 126 female), housed singly in 50 x 30 x 30 cm terraria at 30-32 C by day; all tests from early May to the first ten days of June; null and contrary results in the same section: no significant differences among stimuli in males for general or specific tongue-flick rate; in females no significant differences for interest or chin-rubbing for any compound; in females general tongue-flick rate was higher for the mixture than for the C25 ketone and specific tongue-flick rate higher for the C27 ketone than for the alkane and than for the blank control, with the mixture versus the C27 ketone only near-significant; female models had large numbers of zeros and some parts did not converge (R-hat above 1.05) so the authors urge caution; males: the C25 and C27 ketones each differed from the alkane for interest, mixture versus alkane only near-significant; with compounds grouped, males reacted more to ketones than alkanes for interest and chin-rubbing, females had higher specific tongue-flick rate to ketones than to the control; mean latency to first tongue-flick 291 s (n = 128 tests with tongue-flicking, only those tests included in that statistic); the authors call the response to ketones not very pronounced and hypothesise other compounds make up the female sex pheromone; individuals sometimes left the video frame; numeric estimates are in the supplementary material, which the desk did not read
quote: Thus, C25–C27 ketones provoked stronger reactions in males than C27 alkane, hexane, or the control.
note: Classification: behavioural_response, chin-rubbing and interest on a pheromone-candidate ketone mixture against solvent, alkane and blank controls; the value is limited to the contrasts the paper reports and gives no thresholds or effect sizes (numbers sit in the supplement). The quote's 'C25-C27 ketones' is the equal mixture of the two ketones per the Methods.
